q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
ROAS is not increasing — net ROAS fell while net profit also declined because ad spend grew much faster than contribution margin, so the extra spend erased the margin gains.

Evidence (measured)
- Net ROAS (order-date): 1.27x → 0.87x (−32.0%) — Measured.  
- Net profit (order-date): ₹70,489 → ₹‑96,888 (change −₹1,67,377) — Measured.  
- Ad spend (P&L basis): ₹2,57,516 → ₹7,44,922 (+189.0%) — Measured.  
- Contribution margin: ₹3,28,005 → ₹6,48,034 (+98.0%) — Measured.  

Why that explains it (derived from the data)
- Net profit = Contribution margin − Ad spend: ad spend rose ~189% while contribution rose ~98%, producing the negative net profit. — Derived (accounting identity).
- Net ROAS = Contribution margin ÷ Ad spend: contribution rose but not as fast as ad spend, so ROAS fell. — Derived.

Context: Period compared — previous 2026-09-16..2026-09-29 vs current 2026-09-30..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14.
